title: Pavel Durov on why Telegram would rather leave a market than compromise its principles
summary: After his arrest in France, Durov explains Telegram's stance on privacy versus security. He argues platforms, not CEOs, should be held accountable, says Telegram will exit markets that conflict with its principles, and commits to improving moderation after growth to 950M users.

principles.text: Be willing to leave markets whose demands conflict with your core principles.
principles.quote: We are prepared to leave markets that aren’t compatible with our principles, because we are not doing this for money.

principles.text: Refuse demands that break user trust, even at the cost of being banned.
principles.quote: When Russia demanded we hand over “encryption keys” to enable surveillance, we refused — and Telegram got banned in Russia.

principles.text: Holding founders personally liable for third-party misuse of their tools discourages innovation.
principles.quote: No innovator will ever build new tools if they know they can be personally held responsible for potential abuse of those tools.

principles.text: Rapid user growth creates trust and safety debt; own it and fix it directly.
principles.quote: Telegram’s abrupt increase in user count to 950M caused growing pains that made it easier for criminals to abuse our platform.

principles.text: Keep processes consistent globally while preventing abuse in countries with weak rule of law.
principles.quote: As a platform, you want your processes to be consistent globally, while also ensuring they are not abused in countries with weak rule of law.

principles.text: As founder, take personal ownership of fixing a public problem.
principles.quote: That’s why I made it my personal goal to ensure we significantly improve things in this regard.
